land.text: the Algerian coast and Tell that Cliopatria's Ottoman Empire row (793 Algerian cells, 1560-1705) hands to the Regency in 1706

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws the Regency as a state of its own only from 1706. The page dates it from 1516 ('They captured Algiers in 1516, and Aruj proclaimed himself sultan'; lead '1516 to 1830'), calls it a 'De jure province and vassal state (eyalet) of the Ottoman Empire' that was 'De facto independent since mid-17th century'. Its pre-1706 land is drawn inside the Cliopatria Ottoman Empire row; the Hafsids of Bejaia and the Kingdom of Tlemcen are the page's infobox predecessors.

land.text: Algiers and its surroundings, entered by French troops on 5 July 1830

successors.note: Cliopatria's French Algeria row is 4,234 km2 in 1830-1833 and grows to 211,876 km2 in 1846; the French took Mers-el-Kebir on 14 December 1830 and Oran on 4 January 1831 (Oran page), Bone and Bougie in 1830-1833 (conquest page).

land.text: the unoccupied interior of the Oran province that the Treaty of Desmichels (1834) left to Abd al-Qadir, enlarged by the Treaty of Tafna (1837), Titteri, Miliana, Mascara, Tlemcen, the Sahara around Laghouat, Setif and Biskra

successors.note: The page lists the Emirate (established 27 November 1832) among the Regency's successors. Cliopatria keeps drawing the whole unoccupied remnant as 'Regency of Algiers' until 1845.

land.text: the Beylik of Constantine under Ahmed Bey, repulsed Clauzel in November 1836 and fell to Damremont's expedition in 1837

successors.note: The Regency page names the Beylik of Constantine as a successor state. No dossier or Cliopatria row exists for it; see counterparts_needing_dossiers.

capitals.name: Algiers
capitals.note: Infobox: capital Algiers. The Oran page adds that after the 1792 cession 'The capital was moved there the same year' (the seat of the Bey of the west, not of the Regency).

correction.text: unchanged for 1706-1707, while Spain still held Oran ('Spanish sovereignty lasted until 1708'); from 1708 the regency-of-algiers_1708 keyframe (with Oran) holds

keyframe_review.note: 210,899 km2, 1706-1708, with the Oran enclave left out. The Oran page has the Spanish holding Oran until 1708 ('drive the Spanish out'), so the shape is right for 1706-1707; the 1708 gain is carried by the next keyframe. The Regency page's infobox gives no area (the sanity check is not possible); its text puts the Moroccan frontier on the Moulouya River ('forced to accept the Moulouya River as his eastern border'), the shape's west edge is at 2.12 W (bounding box), close to the modern Algerian-Moroccan frontier; the page does not say whether the line coincides with the river. [Review af-02-f: years limited to 1706-1707 so that the shape does not overlap the 1708 keyframe.]

correction.text: the 1709 shape plus the Oran enclave (Oran, Arzew and the coast to Mers-el-Kebir, six cells), which the Regency held from 1708 to 1732

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Cliopatria leaves Oran out of the Regency in 1709-1791 and adds it only in 1792, but the Oran page has Mustapha Ben Youssef (Bouchelaghem), a vassal of the Deylik of Algiers, driving the Spanish out in 1708 and Spain returning only in 1732. The 1792 Cliopatria shape is used as the carrier of the Oran cells (it differs from the 1709 shape by those six cells and nothing else).

correction.text: unchanged: the 1709 Cliopatria shape without Oran, for the years Oran was Spanish again (1732 to 1792)

keyframe_review.note: The shape stands, but only for 1732-1791: Spain held Oran again from 1732 ('Spanish forces returned under José Carrillo de Albornoz') until the Algerian siege of 1790-1792 and the withdrawal ('By February all Spanish troops had left'). 1709-1731 is replaced by the 1708 keyframe. 210,874 km2, no change elsewhere: the page records no border move with Morocco (Moulouya) or Tunis in these years.

211,975 km2, 1792-1829: Cliopatria adds Oran in 1792, which matches the Oran page (Charles IV 'saw no advantage in continuing the occupation'; agreements with Algiers; troops gone by February). The page does not date the agreements' year; 1792 is the siege heading's last year. No area on the Regency page's infobox.

correction.text: unchanged for 1830, the Regency's last year (French landing 14 June, entry into Algiers 5 July 1830); the Algiers cells French Algeria takes in the same year are drawn by that row

keyframe_review.note: The shape (207,542 km2, 1830-1833) is the Regency minus the 15 cells of Cliopatria's French Algeria, and is kept for 1830 only. The invasion page: 'Annexation of Algiers by France and collapse of the Regency of Algiers' (14 June - 5 July 1830). For 1831-1833 the same cells are the interior after the collapse: see the 1834 verdict.

correction.text: not the Regency, which collapsed in July 1830: the unoccupied remainder of Algeria, to be drawn under the successors (the Emirate of Abdelkader from 27 November 1832, the Beylik of Constantine, Kabylia and the Saharan oases)

keyframe_review.note: 196,606 km2, 1834-1839. The Regency ended in 1830 (invasion page). The conquest page has France 'formally annexed the occupied areas of Algeria' in 1834 and, by the Treaty of Desmichels, 'recognized Abdelkader as the sovereign of territories in Oran province not under French control'; the Emirate page lists its provinces (Titteri, Miliana, Tlemcen, Mascara, Sahara, Mejdana, Ziban, Jibal). Cliopatria keeps the unoccupied remainder under the Regency's name; the emirate-of-abdelkader dossier takes it from this shape.

correction.text: the unoccupied remainder of Algeria, belonging to the Emirate of Abdelkader (after the Treaty of Tafna, May 1837, 'effectively recognized Abd al-Qadir's control over much of the interior') and the Beylik of Constantine until its fall in 1837

keyframe_review.note: Same cells as 1834 (196,606 km2, 1836-1839). Conquest page: Clauzel occupied Tlemcen in January 1836, repulsed at Constantine in November 1836, Constantine taken in 1837, Tafna in May 1837. The Regency no longer exists.

correction.text: the unoccupied remainder of Algeria in the war resumed in late 1839: the Emirate of Abdelkader's interior

keyframe_review.note: 182,085 km2, 1840-1841, 14,500 km2 smaller than 1834 as French Algeria's row grows from 15,320 to 29,467 km2. Conquest page: 'Abdelkader renewed the jihad' after the French marched through the Iron Gates (late 1839); Bugeaud replaced Valee in December 1840.

correction.text: the unoccupied remainder of Algeria in the last years of the Emirate of Abdelkader (surrender December 1847)

keyframe_review.note: 163,274 km2, 1842-1845, shrinking as French Algeria reaches 48,573 km2 in 1842. Conquest page: the Smala raid of 1843, the 1844 Treaty of Tangier with Morocco, Abdelkader's surrender in December 1847. Cliopatria's Regency row stops in 1845 and French Algeria's 1846 shape (211,876 km2) covers the whole country.

region.text: the Regency of Algiers as Cliopatria draws it from 1706: the Algerian Tell and coast with the Moulouya River as its western frontier

ledger.note: 1706: the Regency of Algiers, in being since 1516 and 'de facto independent since mid-17th century', is drawn as a state of its own. The year is Cliopatria's, not the page's: the lead gives '1516 to 1830' ('They captured Algiers in 1516, and Aruj proclaimed himself sultan'), an eyalet 'under Suleiman I in spring 1521', pashas from 1587, aghas after 1659 and deys after 1671. Until 1705 the same land is inside Cliopatria's Ottoman Empire row.

region.text: Oran, which the Spanish had held since Pedro Navarro's conquest of 17 May 1509

ledger.note: 1708: Oran falls to the Regency. Mustapha Ben Youssef (Bouchelaghem), 'vassal of the Deylik of Algiers', took advantage of the War of Spanish Succession to drive the Spanish out of Oran; the page gives no month. Cliopatria's 1709 shape leaves Oran out.

1710: the dey takes the title of pasha. 'From 1710 the deys assumed the title of pasha at the initiative of Dey Baba Ali Chaouch' (the page's text breaks off in this sentence); the state and its land are unchanged.

region.text: Oran, captured by Spanish forces in 1732

ledger.note: 1732: Spain retakes Oran. 'Spanish forces returned under José Carrillo de Albornoz' and captured the city from Bouchelaghem; the page links him to the Duke of Montemar and gives no month.

region.text: Oran, besieged by the Bey Mohammed el Kebir

ledger.note: 1790: the Algerian siege of Oran begins. After another earthquake damaged the Spanish defences (the page dates a violent one to the night after 8 October 1790), Mohammed el Kebir, the new Bey of Oran, besieged the city, and by the end of 1790 the Algerians had a clear advantage; the page heads the section 1790-1792 and does not narrate 1791.

region.text: Oran, from which the Spanish troops withdrew by February

ledger.note: 1792: the siege ends in the Spanish withdrawal. Charles IV 'saw no advantage in continuing the occupation' and opened talks with the Dey; agreements were signed 'on 12 September in Algiers, and on 12 December in Madrid' (the page gives no year) and 'By February all Spanish troops had left'.

region.text: Oran, ceded by Charles IV to the Dey of Algiers

ledger.note: 1792: Spain cedes Oran to the Regency and the Bey's capital is moved there 'the same year'. Cliopatria adds the Oran cells to the Regency's shape in 1792; the year is the siege heading's and Cliopatria's, the month is the page's ('By February all Spanish troops had left').

region.text: Algiers and the coast where the French landed

ledger.note: 14 June 1830: the French invasion of Algiers begins. The infobox dates the invasion '14 June - 5 July 1830'; French forces under Bourmont and the fleet under Duperre fought the Algerian forces of Hussein Dey, whose beys of Oran, Titteri and Medea answered the call to arms and gathered at Staoueli.
5 July 1830: the fighting ends. 'French troops entered the city on July 5 at 12:00.'

region.text: Algiers and its surroundings, which French troops entered on 5 July 1830

ledger.note: 5 July 1830: Algiers passes to France. 'French troops entered the city on July 5 at 12:00'; Bourmont had demanded the city, the fleet, the treasury and the departure of the Turks. The cells are Cliopatria's French Algeria shape of 1830 (4,234 km2); the page names the city, not its hinterland.

region.text: the Regency of Algiers in its last year

ledger.note: July 1830: the Regency of Algiers falls. The infobox lists 'Annexation of Algiers by France and collapse of the Regency of Algiers'; 'A few days later, Hussein Dey and his family embarked on a frigate and departed for Naples'. The rest of the country (the beyliks of Oran, Titteri and Constantine) is left without a central government; Cliopatria keeps drawing it as the Regency until 1845.

wars.name: Moroccan invasions of Algeria under Moulay Ismail
wars.outcome: The Moroccan invasions of 1678, 1692, 1701 and 1707 failed and Moulay Ismail 'was forced to accept the Moulouya River as his eastern border with Ottoman Algeria'.
wars.note: Only the 1701 and 1707 invasions fall in Cliopatria's span; no ground changed hands, so no zone is given. The frontier on the Moulouya is the Regency's west edge.

wars.name: Spanish-Algerian wars for Oran

zones.text: Oran, taken by the Algerians in 1708, retaken by Spain in 1732 and ceded in 1792

wars.outcome: Oran changed hands three times: Algerian in 1708, Spanish again in 1732, Algerian for good after the siege of 1790-1792.
wars.note: The page narrates the 1708 and 1732 changes in one line each and the 1790 earthquake and siege in a paragraph; 1791 is not narrated.

wars.name: Barbary Wars
belligerents: the naval powers of the Barbary Wars (the page names none)
wars.outcome: The page calls the Barbary Wars (1785-1816) the point where Algiers was 'decisively defeated for the first time'; no territorial change.
wars.note: Listed so that the reviewer can see it was considered; the page gives no territory moved and no treaty year.

wars.name: Invasion of Algiers in 1830

zones.text: Algiers and the coast where the French landed

wars.outcome: French victory: Algiers taken on 5 July 1830, Hussein Dey exiled to Naples and the Regency collapsed.
wars.note: Cause per the page: the 1827 fly-whisk incident and a three-year blockade. 14 June - 5 July 1830.

wars.name: French conquest of Algeria
wars.outcome: France took the coast piecemeal (Oran and Bone 1830-31, Bejaia 1833, Constantine 1837), made peace with Abd al-Qadir at Desmichels (1834) and Tafna (May 1837), resumed war in late 1839 and ended the Emirate with his surrender in December 1847.
wars.note: After 5 July 1830 the fighting is waged by the Regency's successors; their contest events belong to emirate-of-abdelkader and french-algeria, so no zone is given here.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line is on the pages: the Moroccan frontier on the Moulouya River is a river, not a surveyed line; Touggourt and Ouargla were tributaries 'until 1830'; the Tunisian and Saharan frontiers are unrecorded.

sources.title: Regency of Algiers
sources.note: Identity, 1516 origin, infobox, 1710 pasha title, Moulouya frontier. The page text is cut off by the fetch tool in the 1710 sentence, so 1710-1830 had to come from other pages.

sources.title: Invasion of Algiers in 1830
sources.note: Dates of the invasion, entry into Algiers 5 July 1830, collapse of the Regency, Hussein Dey's exile.

sources.title: French conquest of Algeria
sources.note: Post-1830 phases: Oran/Bone 1830-31, Bejaia 1833, Desmichels 1834, annexation 1834, Constantine 1836-37, Tafna 1837, war resumed 1839-40, Smala 1843, Abdelkader's surrender December 1847.

sources.title: Oran
sources.note: Oran under Spain and Algiers: 1708, 1732, 1790-1792, French occupation 1830-31.

notes: Regency of Algiers (af-02-f). (1) Start: the Regency dates from 1516 (lead '1516 to 1830', Algiers taken that year, an eyalet from spring 1521, 'De facto independent since mid-17th century'), but Cliopatria draws it as its own row only from 1706 and the same land (793 Algerian cells, 1560-1705) sits in the Cliopatria Ottoman Empire row. The dossier starts in 1706 so that the two rows do not overlap; the found event is confidence 1. The ottoman-empire dossier (me-10) should record the Regency as a vassal (the page: 'De jure province and vassal state (eyalet)') from 1706 and may wish to draw 1516-1705 as a state of its own; no page was opened for 1516-1705 beyond the Regency's own text. (2) The Regency page is truncated by the fetch tool in the middle of the 1710 sentence ('who strangled seventeen hundre'), so 1710-1830 rests on the Oran, invasion and conquest pages; the Tunis and Moroccan frontiers, the beys of Constantine and Titteri, the wars of 1756, 1807 and 1813-1814 with Tunis and the Tuareg south are not on any page opened (page budget); the shapes show no border move for them. (3) Oran: Cliopatria leaves it out of the Regency in 1709-1791 and adds it in 1792; the Oran page has the Algerians holding it 1708-1732, so a 1708-1731 keyframe adds it. The Spain-Algiers agreements are given as '12 September in Algiers, and on 12 December in Madrid' without a year; 1792 is the siege heading's. (4) 1830-1845: the Regency fell on 5 July 1830, but Cliopatria keeps a 'Regency of Algiers' shape to 1845 that is the unconquered remainder of Algeria (French Algeria's row is the conquered part: the two rows never overlap, and French Algeria's 1846 shape of 211,876 km2 equals the whole 1792 Regency shape). The verdicts mark 1834-1842 wrong and 1830 adjust (kept for 1830 only). The remainder needs owners: emirate-of-abdelkader (written in this batch), the Beylik of Constantine (Ahmed Bey; no dossier), Kabylia and the Saharan oases (Touggourt, Ouargla, Laghouat); until they exist, 1831-1845 land outside French Algeria and the Emirate is stateless. (5) Rulers omitted: the page lists only Aruj, Baba Ali Chaouch, Baba Mohammed ben-Osman and Hussein Dey with partial years. French sequence after 1830 (Mers-el-Kebir 14 December 1830, Oran 4 January 1831, Tlemcen January 1836) is in french-algeria's remit; the Oran page gives both dates.
